# Calculating the Vassiliev Invariant for Knot K₁

## Identifying the Knot

The knot **K₁** in standard knot theory problems is the **trefoil knot** (the simplest non-trivial knot), which has 3 crossings.

## Vassiliev Invariants – Background

Vassiliev (finite-type) invariants are defined via singular knots. For **knots** (single-component links):

| Type | Value |
|------|-------|
| 0 | 1 (constant) |
| 1 | 0 (vanishes for all knots) |
| 2 | 0 (vanishes for all knots) |
| **3** | **First non-trivial** |

The first non-trivial finite-type invariant for a knot is of **type 3**, and it is extracted from the **Conway polynomial**:

$$\nabla_K(z) = 1 + a_2\, z^2 + a_4\, z^4 + \cdots$$

> **Theorem:** The coefficient $a_{2n}(K)$ is a Vassiliev invariant of type $2n+1$.

## Computing the Conway Polynomial of the Trefoil

Using the skein relation for the Conway polynomial:
$$\nabla_{L_+}(z) - \nabla_{L_-}(z) = z\,\nabla_{L_0}(z)$$

Resolving the trefoil crossings step by step:

1. $\nabla_{\text{trefoil}}(z) - \nabla_{\text{unknot}}(z) = z\,\nabla_{\text{Hopf link resolution}}(z)$
2. Working through the resolutions gives:

$$\nabla_{\text{trefoil}}(z) = 1 + z^2$$

Therefore:
$$a_0 = 1, \qquad a_2 = 1$$

## Extracting the Vassiliev Invariant

The coefficient $a_2 = 1$ is the **type-3 Vassiliev invariant** — the first non-trivial finite-type invariant for the trefoil:

$$v_3(K_1) = a_2 = 1$$

## Result

$$\boxed{1}$$
